ds: Accounts that collect deposits from many locations, often in different geographic areas, and funnel the money onward, frequently to another jurisdiction, so as to avoid direct links with the criminal source. They are commonly used in drug trafficking and fraud cash networks.

src.t: FATF, Money Laundering through the Physical Transportation of Cash (2015)
FFIEC, BSA/AML Examination Manual (FinCEN is not publisher)

cn.rt: Funnel accounts take geographically dispersed cash deposits and move funds on fast; retail accounts with branch deposits and digital onward transfer.

rat: Multi-location cash deposits and rapid ATM withdrawals elsewhere on retail accounts.

ind.n: Cash deposits from many states or regions
ind.cx: Account receives cash deposits across geographically distant locations from the account holder's home area.
ind.ds: Account receives cash deposits across geographically distant locations from the account holder's home area.

ind.n: Rapid withdrawals following deposits in different location
ind.cx: Funds credited in one area are withdrawn quickly elsewhere, often by ATM.
ind.ds: Cash deposited is quickly withdrawn or transferred onward, including to another location or to unhosted wallets.
ind.cn: Rapid onward movement after cash credits

ind.cx: No salary, bills, or everyday spending, only deposits and withdrawals.
ind.fp: New or secondary accounts have limited use.
ind.ds: No salary, bills, or everyday spending, only deposits and withdrawals.

ind.n: Individual or business holder lacks economic link to deposit areas
ind.cx: Account holder profile shows no business or family ties in places where deposits occur.
ind.fp: Customers may be mobile or have remote clients.
ind.ds: Account holder profile shows no business or family ties in places where deposits occur.

ind.n: Multiple unrelated depositors to same account
ind.cx: Numerous third parties deposit into one account, sometimes with slips or reference.
ind.ds: Numerous unconnected individuals make deposits into the same account, often in similar amounts or within short windows.
ind.cn: Many unrelated depositors paying into one account

ind.n: Funds sent offshore soon after collection
ind.cx: Aggregated funds are wired or sent through remittance to foreign jurisdictions.
ind.fp: International students and migrants send funds abroad.
ind.ds: Aggregated funds are wired or sent through remittance to foreign jurisdictions.

ind.n: Account opened with limited documentation or by recruited individuals
ind.cx: Account holders include students, unemployed people or newcomers sharing similar addresses.
ind.ds: Account holders include students, unemployed people or newcomers sharing similar addresses.

ind.n: Use of cash deposit machines and cards across multiple accounts
ind.cx: Debit cards or deposit tokens shared or sent to others to deposit.
ind.ds: Debit cards or deposit tokens shared or sent to others to deposit.

ctl.n: Cash deposit profiling and peer benchmarking
ctl.ds: Compares cash deposits and withdrawals with expected activity, sector and location peers and declared turnover, alerting on outliers. It helps find cash that is inconsistent with the stated business.

ctl.n: Fan-in, fan-out and funnel account detection
ctl.ds: Detects accounts receiving from many unrelated senders, or sending to many beneficiaries, followed by consolidation or onward movement. It surfaces collector, funnel and mule structures.

Alerts on unusual countries, corridors, deposit locations and geolocation dispersion relative to the customer profile or on activity near designated risk regions. It focuses review on geographic anomalies.

ctl.n: Funds hold, freeze and recall procedure
ctl.ds: Provides a defined, legally grounded capability to restrict, hold, freeze or recall funds and accounts pending review or on confirmed exposure, with clear triggers and approvers. It stops onward dissipation of suspected illicit funds.
Model that scores inbound-then-outbound pass-through, new-payee churn, counterparty diversity and profile mismatch to flag likely mule accounts. It prioritises accounts for review and restriction.

ctl.n: Purpose and intended nature of relationship
ctl.ds: Captures and challenges the stated purpose of the account, expected activity, volumes and geographies at onboarding, creating a baseline against which later behaviour is judged. Vague or implausible answers prompt further enquiry or decline.

Contacts the customer, or the relationship manager does so, to obtain and record an explanation of unusual transactions, relationships or recipients, and to test it against evidence. The answer informs whether activity is legitimate or should be escalated.

Compares actual activity with the customer's declared profile, history and peers and alerts on material or trend-breaking deviation, usually as a contextual signal. It catches change that rules on fixed thresholds miss.

Detects, restricts and challenges payments or deposits made by or to parties not named in the contract, account or invoice, and requires evidence of the relationship. It stops accounts and trades being funded by unexplained third parties.
Alerts when inflows are quickly moved out with little retained balance, including cash-in fast-out and rapid conversion or cash-out. It reveals accounts used as conduits for layering.

Applies additional information gathering, corroboration, monitoring and senior review to relationships or transactions assessed as higher risk, covering purpose, expected activity, ownership and funds. The depth is proportionate to the risk drivers identified.
Links accounts, devices, addresses, directors and beneficiaries to surface rings, shared attributes and flow structures that single-account views miss. It supports detection of organised networks.
Clusters customers, vendors and entities that share addresses, phones, devices, officers or bank details, including against staff records. It reveals common control and hidden relationships.

Caps transaction size, frequency, load, withdrawal and deposit values, with staged increases as legitimate behaviour is established and per-customer limits at kiosks. It bounds the loss and laundering capacity of new or higher-risk accounts.
